body.statement: When \(d=1\), the confidence rule in Definition \(\mathrm{def:simultaneous\text{-}rule}\) forms \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_n=B_1\) by jointly inverting both fixed-kernel residual-HSIC intervals and the cross-fitted conditional-risk intervals used in the GENE scores: a candidate \(b\in\{-1,+1\}\) is retained exactly when the interval for \(H_{1,b}\) contains \(0\), the interval for \(H_{1,-b}\) intersects \([\lambda,\infty)\), and the lower confidence bound for \(s_{1,b}-s_{1,-b}\) is nonnegative, with the defined two-direction fallback if this set is empty. The corresponding population rule selects the unique zero-HSIC direction from Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:population\text{-}direction\text{-}margin}\) while enforcing the GENE score comparison. If Open-ended Question \(\mathrm{oeq:uniform\text{-}generated\text{-}residual\text{-}expansion}\) is resolved affirmatively for \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\) and \(\mathcal G_n(x;C_m,\widehat m)\), and the nuisance condition in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:uniform\text{-}minimax\text{-}frontier}\) holds at its displayed \(n_0\), then \(N^*(1,\alpha,\lambda)\asymp\lambda^{-1}\log(2/\alpha)\).
body.justification: This verifies that the \(d=1\) restriction is the bivariate joint GENE--residual-HSIC inversion actually defined by the proposal and has the intended local sample-complexity scale.
body.gap: Mooij et al. (2016) establish consistency for this bivariate rule but not its local finite-sample sample-complexity expression.
body.consumer: Single-pair benchmark users obtain a calibrated special case and a direct check on implementation.
